pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migration 0002 adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js AC-1 checks existing rows normal and 'urgent' rejected.
AC-2 test asserts exact labelled list with normal unlabelled.
AC-3 test checks high/low/normal filters in id order.
AC-4 test checks unfiltered list in id order.
AC-5 test asserts exact nav for all four views.
AC-6 test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty, __proto__.
AC-7 test checks exact messages for no-match and empty table across all views.
routes.json contains /?priority=high; AC-8 test asserts it; traffic worker fetches ROUTES paths.

findings.what: The last commit 'Follow-up edits' loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns null when absent, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The state-table row 'No match' is then only checked by the AC-7 test.
findings.fix: Restore expect(message(html)).toBe("No low-priority items.") in the 'No match' state test.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but commit d4414ca loosened an assertion in the No match state test.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or disclose the loosening in the PR with its justification.

lenses.note: A spec exists and the change follows it. Both decisions are respected (existing items normal; only high and low labelled). Nothing extra beyond the traffic-check regex relaxation, which AC-8 needs.
All 8 ACs are named by tests. The 'No match' state test was weakened in the last commit, but AC-7 still covers the exact messages.
The tests are mostly behavioural. One assertion (toBeDefined on message()) can never fail. I did not run the tests; CI runs them.
README mentions the filter. The README does not describe the 400 response or the labels, which is minor.
The src/index.js logic is correct. Invalid or empty priority returns 400, and the query is parameterised.
The priority value is whitelisted and bound as a parameter. Titles are escaped. The priority value is only interpolated into HTML after passing the whitelist.
The page is minimal HTML with a nav; no further issues found.
No browser flow was demonstrated, but the tests cover rendered HTML. Nothing further to report.
The claim that no tests were loosened is false (see finding). Other claims match the diff.
